angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 582,997 km at 28.64 pc = 0.27 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 52521: distance 28.636 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 28.636 +/- 0.258 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 35.1056 +/- 0.0212 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01), 1653.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 0.838 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 52521: radius 0.838 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.387 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 582,997 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4976 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 52521: effective temperature 4976 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.026) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 52521: effective temperature 4976 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.026) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 93083 (pscomppars): spectral type K2 IV-V, from Stoeva et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A.232S/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 93083: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 93083 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.13 dex, from Stoeva et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A.232S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 93083 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.39041, from Stoeva et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A.232S/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 93083 (pscomppars): age 10.71 Gyr, from Stoeva et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A.232S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 93083 (pscomppars): rotation period 32.3 d, from Stoeva et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A.232S/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 93083 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.9 km/s, from Lovis et al. 2005 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2005A&A...437.1121L/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.838 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.686. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4.24 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 18 published values span log g 4.16 to 4.57, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
